messages:
alex: Quick check — I'm rolling a Terraform change that flips our service to a multi-port Service (grpc+metrics) behind an NLB. Noticed ALB/NLB SNI handling looks weird when the same IP hosts multiple TLS certs. Anyone seen fallback certs get picked up incorrectly?

maria: Oof. We recently hit something similar when using the aws annotation for sni-preserve. In our case ALB will pick the first host cert if the SNI isn't present, which broke metric scraping.

sanjay: Can you paste the Service + Ingress/Gateway config you're applying? Might be an annotation ordering or gateway-api TLS binding issue.

alex: Here's the k8s Service snippet (applied via terraform k8s_manifest):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-backend
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-additional-resource-tags: "team=infra"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
    - name: grpc
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
    - name: metrics
      port: 9443
      targetPort: 9090
  selector:
    app: inference
```

alex: Terraform diff also adds this annotation we copied from a sample: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: arn:aws:acm:...:alb-cert`

jon: If you're using NLB with TLS passthrough, the NLB doesn't look at SNI for cert selection — that happens upstream. Are you mixing NLB passthrough + ALB TLS terminate?

maria: ^ this. Also check if gateway-api TCPRoute is doing host-based routing. For TLS terminate on ALB, SNI mapping is based on ALB listener rules; mixing multiport on same LB IP can confuse things if listeners overlap.

alex: We're using NLB passthrough for port 443 (grpc), but metrics I'd like to TLS terminate at the ALB for LB healthchecks + Prom scrape. The Terraform change sets two different load balancers via annotations (legacy hack). Trying to avoid creating extra IPs.

sanjay: Two observations: 1) Running two LBs against the same Service via annotations is brittle. 2) If you must, ensure distinct listeners and that certificates are bound to the correct listeners. AWS might reuse the cert if listener rules are ambiguous.

jon: Could we instead: keep a single NLB for grpc (passthrough), expose metrics via a ClusterIP + a separate ALB Service that points to a metrics-only Deployment in same namespace? That keeps L7 TLS termination isolated.

alex: That would add a second Service + small infra but sounds cleaner. My concern is Terraform churn and IP quota.

maria: Alternative: use Gateway API and two TLSRoutes/TCPRoutes with explicit hostname matching and different TLSCertificate resources. Gateway controller should create distinct listeners. Might be a medium effort refactor.

alex: For the short term I'll revert the extra annotation and split metrics into a ClusterIP + NodePort behind existing ALB we already have for observability. Can someone review the terraform plan before I apply? cc @sanjay @jon :eyes:

sanjay: Happy to review — post the plan link. Quick checklist: ensure target group protocol matches (tls vs tcp), healthcheck port is right, and annotation keys are exact (no stray dash).

jon: I'll run a quick load test once applied to catch any fallback certs. Also add a canary tag so we can route 10% of traffic to the new config first. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-plan: terraform apply queued by alex for module=infra/k8s-service, change_id=chg-9821. Run `tf plan` link: https://ci.internal/builds/9821

alex: Thanks all — I'll update the PR with the split-service approach and ping this thread with the plan URL.

maria: Thanks — and if you want me to clean up old annotations in a follow-up PR I can do that to avoid surprises. :sparkles:

alex: Perfect. I'll hold the apply until reviews + canary configured.
